title: Dominic and the Harbor
premise: In 1911, Edmund Ashgrove, an apprentice clockmaker who has spent her life passing as a man to keep her trade, is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock in the harbor town of Vell. While working inside its mechanism she finds documents proving the harbor master falsified tide ledgers to cover a wreck he caused — a wreck that killed her father. When winter closes the bridge and traps her in Vell, Edmund must decide whether to stay invisible or smuggle the evidence past three checkpoints before the harbor master destroys it at season's end. She succeeds at devastating cost: exposed as a woman and disowned by her guild, she leaves across the ice with the truth delivered, finally belonging to herself rather than to any town, trade, or name.
about_author: Isandro Joubert is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing tide ledgers and lighthouse logs along the northern coast. Their fiction explores how ordinary people carry unbearable knowledge across impossible distances.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Edmund Ashgrove, disguised as a male apprentice clockmaker, receives the summons to repair the observatory's master clock in distant Vell. She packs light, measuring her life in what can be carried. POV: Edmund. Beat: restless ambition shadowed by the fear of being discovered.

chapters.title: Arrival at Falling Tide
chapters.summary: Edmund reaches Vell as the last ferry departs for the season. The town is gray, watchful, and obsessed with the sea. She glimpses the harbor master, Corven Hale, whose grief-stricken public face unsettles her. POV: Edmund. Beat: unease beneath professional focus.

chapters.title: The Heart of the Observatory
chapters.summary: Inside the observatory, Edmund opens the master clock's case and finds it sabotaged — deliberately, recently. Hidden among the works are tide ledgers contradicting official records from the night of the Wrenwreck five years ago. POV: Edmund. Beat: cold shock; the past knocking through brass and steel.

chapters.title: Her Father's Name
chapters.summary: Edmund deciphers the ledgers: Hale falsified tide readings that lured her father's pilot boat onto the rocks. She realizes the sabotage was meant to hide them until spring. POV: Edmund. Beat: grief crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Edmund maps her problem: the bridge is closed; the only way out is past the customs house, the ferry office, and Hale's own gate when the ice road opens. She begins copying evidence. POV: Edmund. Beat: methodical dread.

chapters.title: The Landlady Who Sees
chapters.summary: Her landlady, Mrs. Tarnow, notices Edmund's hands and sleepless eyes but says nothing — yet. A fragile alliance forms over shared tea and unasked questions. POV: Edmund. Beat: the terror and comfort of being perceived.

chapters.title: Hale's Repair
chapters.summary: Hale commissions Edmund to fix his study clock, giving her access to his home. She finds the original true ledger hidden there — and his private shrine to the drowned, including her father's pocket watch. POV: Edmund. Beat: horror braided with unexpected pity.

chapters.title: A Town That Remembers
chapters.summary: Vell's annual memorial for the Wrenwreck reveals the town's divided memory: some blame Hale, some worship him. Edmund listens, learning who might help and who would betray her. POV: Edmund. Beat: belonging offered on false terms.

chapters.title: The Boy at the Ferry Office
chapters.summary: Edmund befriends Piet, a teenage clerk at the ferry office checkpoint, trading clock repairs for gossip about the ice road's opening date. He idolizes Hale. POV: Edmund. Beat: guilt over using kindness as a tool.

chapters.title: First Search
chapters.summary: Customs officers, tipped anonymously, search lodgings for 'a thief of harbor papers.' Mrs. Tarnow hides Edmund's copies inside a quilt without being asked. POV: Edmund. Beat: gratitude sharpening into resolve — she is no longer alone.

chapters.title: What the Clock Keeps
chapters.summary: Edmund repairs the master clock fully and discovers Hale visits it nightly, winding it himself — a penance ritual. She realizes he knows someone found the ledgers. POV: Edmund. Beat: hunter and hunted exchanging places.

chapters.title: Piet's Doubt
chapters.summary: Edmund shows Piet one page, not naming herself. His faith in Hale cracks as arithmetic contradicts the official story. POV: Edmund. Beat: dangerous hope that truth can recruit allies.

chapters.title: The Ice Road Forms
chapters.summary: The harbor freezes; the ice road to the mainland will open within days. Hale announces he'll burn old records 'for tidiness' at season's end. POV: Edmund. Beat: the clock running down.

chapters.title: Mrs. Tarnow's Confession
chapters.summary: Mrs. Tarnow reveals she saw the Wrenwreck from her window and was paid to stay silent. She gives Edmund her testimony. POV: Edmund. Beat: two women choosing courage over safety together.

chapters.title: Unmasked
chapters.summary: Hale confronts Edmund privately: he has known she's a woman since her first week — and suspected why she came. He offers passage out if she leaves the papers. POV: Edmund. Beat: identity weaponized against her; temptation of erasure.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Edmund refuses, telling him her father's name aloud for the first time in years. Hale, shaken, doesn't report her — yet. POV: Edmund. Beat: claiming selfhood at the edge of ruin.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Gate
chapters.summary: Piet, torn between idols, tells Hale about the copied pages — but not about Edmund. The search narrows. Edmund must move tonight, ahead of schedule. POV: Edmund. Beat: betrayal that still carries mercy.

chapters.title: Across the Frozen Harbor
chapters.summary: Edmund crosses the ice at night toward the customs house checkpoint, pursued, carrying the originals sewn into her coat. The ice groans and shifts. POV: Edmund. Beat: pure survival terror.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: Customs
chapters.summary: Caught at the customs house, Edmund gambles everything: she opens her coat before they do, declaring the papers and her name publicly. The customs officer, an old friend of her father, hesitates. POV: Edmund. Beat: exposure as liberation.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Ferry Office
chapters.summary: Piet stands guard at the second checkpoint. He lets her pass, then follows — choosing to witness rather than obey. POV: Edmund. Beat: forgiveness extended and received.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: Hale's Gate
chapters.summary: At the final gate, Hale waits alone. Instead of stopping her, he hands her the true ledger's missing final page — his confession — and watches her walk out of his life. POV: Edmund. Beat: climax resolving not in victory but in mutual reckoning.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: On the mainland, the evidence ends Hale's career and clears her father's name. Disowned by the guild once her disguise is known, Edmund opens a small repair shop under her own name, keeping the master clock's broken escapement on her shelf. POV: Edmund. Beat: quiet resolution — belonging found not in a place, but in a self finally whole.
